<div class="callout-note" role="note">
<h2>Get this information in a different format</h2>
<p><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/standards-and-guidance/nz-government-web-standards/digital-accessibility-standard#alt">View available alternate formats</a></p>
</div>
<h2>About the standard</h2>
<p>The New Zealand Government Web Standards currently include the Web Accessibility Standard and the Web Usability Standard.</p>
<p>A <a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/standards-and-guidance/nz-government-web-standards/digital-accessibility-standard/draft-das">new Digital Accessibility Standard (DAS)</a> will replace the Web Accessibility Standard in early 2027.</p>
<p>The new standard is being created with the people who need it — disabled people and those who create digital information and services for government.</p>
<h3>Timeline for implementation</h3>
<p>The standard is being drafted and there will be a public consultation from Monday 13 July to Friday 7 August 2026.</p>
<p>The standard will be published in early 2027, along with a document explaining how and why decisions were made.</p>
<p>The standard will become official soon after that.</p>
<p>Key dates:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/standards-and-guidance/nz-government-web-standards/digital-accessibility-standard/das-consultation">July to August 2026 — public consultation</a></li>
<li>Early 2027 — consultation summary published</li>
<li>Early 2027 — support programmes published</li>
<li>Early 2027 — Standard published.</li>
</ul>
<h2>What the standard will cover</h2>
<p>The Web Accessibility Standard applies only to websites and web apps. The proposed DAS is likely to apply to all information and communication technology (ICT). This includes:</p>
<ul>
<li>websites, mobile apps, and non-web documents like PDFs, spreadsheets, and emails</li>
<li>non-web software like operating systems or Microsoft Word</li>
<li>hardware, from laptops and headsets to printers and kiosks.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Who must follow the standard</h2>
<p>We’re still confirming which government agencies will have to meet the DAS. All government agencies are strongly encouraged to follow the standard.</p>
<h3>Helping government agencies meet the DAS</h3>
<p>We’re also planning support activities to help government agencies improve digital accessibility and meet the standard. We’re developing these with Whaikaha - Ministry of Disabled People.</p>
<h2>Why we need a new standard</h2>
<p>We’re changing the standard to make sure that accessibility is considered for all digital technology — something the current standard does not do.</p>
<p>All government digital information and services, not just websites, must be accessible to disabled people. This expectation is set out in New Zealand’s Human Rights Act and in the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.</p>
<p>The DAS will help government to meet these responsibilities by setting clear rules for digital accessibility, along with support to help agencies put them into effect.</p>
<h2>How we created the new standard</h2>
<p>The draft DAS has been developed using findings from the 2025 <a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/digital-government/strategy/insights-and-commentary/accessible-digital-government-services-for-new-zealand">Accessible Digital Government Services for New Zealand research</a>. The research highlighted government organisations’ need for guidance and support to put the standard into action.</p>
<p>The draft DAS has also been informed by talking with:</p>
<ul>
<li><span lang="mi">Whaikaha</span> - Ministry of Disabled People</li>
<li>Disabled People’s Organisations</li>
<li>disabled people</li>
<li>public and private sector digital practitioners like designers, developers, and testers</li>
<li>decision-makers and leaders.</li>
</ul>
<h2>What will happen to the Web Usability Standard</h2>
<p>The requirements of the Web Usability Standard will be incorporated into other standards and guidance.</p>
<p>If you have any questions about what is on this page, please email <a href="mailto:web.standards@gdda.govt.nz?subject=Question%20about%20the%20Digital%20Accessibility%20Standard">web.standards@gdda.govt.nz</a>.</p>
<h2 id="alt">Alternate formats</h2>
<p>All the information about the DAS is available in the following formats:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/assets/Standards-guidance/NZ-government-web-standards/DAS/Digital-Accessibility-Standard-DAS-Large-print.pdf">Large print (PDF 210KB)</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/assets/Standards-guidance/NZ-government-web-standards/DAS/Digital-Accessibility-Standard-DAS-Large-print.docx">Large print (DOCX 591KB)</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/assets/Standards-guidance/NZ-government-web-standards/DAS/Digital-Accessibility-Standard-DAS-Braille.brf">Braille (BRF 12KB)</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/assets/Standards-guidance/NZ-government-web-standards/DAS/Digital-Accessibility-Standard-DAS-Easy-Read.pdf">Easy Read (PDF 2.7MB)</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/assets/Standards-guidance/NZ-government-web-standards/DAS/Digital-Accessibility-Standard-DAS-Easy-Read.docx">Easy Read (DOCX 10MB)</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gwifLDrzQ0g">New Zealand Sign Language (NZSL) — YouTube</a></li>
<li>Audio — coming soon</li>
</ul>
